expectations_used.clarify: Reads the failing test body and asks whether partially shipped holds should return only unshipped units before editing.
expectations_used.approach: Names the mechanism — the sweep releasing the original count rather than the remaining count — not merely "something in the sweep".
expectations_used.communicate: Narrates what the failure diff shows and which hold-state fields are being traced.
expectations_used.implement: Changes the sweep's released-quantity computation to test the stated hypothesis.
expectations_used.verify: Re-runs the suite and confirms the partially-shipped expiry test passes without breaking full-release behavior.
expectations_used.reflect: Explains why releasing the original count created phantom stock and how the remaining-count fix prevents it.

summary: The candidate quickly read the failing test, correctly diagnosed the exact mechanism (sweep releasing original count instead of remaining), and made a single edit to sweep.ts. They never re-ran the test suite afterward, ending the session on an unverified declaration of confidence.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate opened and read the failing test before forming any hypothesis, and used the diff (expected five vs got eight) to reason about the bug rather than guessing blind. They did not explicitly ask a clarifying question, but the test evidence they cited resolved the ambiguity themselves, so no unstated assumption was acted upon.

Before touching any code, the candidate stated the precise mechanism — the sweep releasing the original unit count rather than the remaining count — which matches the actual planted bug almost verbatim. This is a specific, falsifiable hypothesis, not just a vague location.

The candidate narrated the failure diff and their hypothesis clearly at two points before editing, giving the interviewer a followable thread. However, narration stopped after that — no commentary during the edit itself or on why the change was sufficient.

The edit to sweep.ts was made directly in line with the stated plan and was saved without visible thrashing or unrelated changes. Since there was only one edit and no observed pushback, it's hard to credit deeper adaptive skill, but it was coherent and appropriately scoped.

After saving the fix, the candidate declared confidence and ended the session without re-running the test suite to confirm the previously failing test now passed or that other behavior wasn't broken. This is a direct miss of the verification bar for this problem.

The candidate's closing statement was a vague expression of confidence rather than an explanation connecting the fix to the root cause or confirming outcome via test results. Since no verification occurred, there was no basis offered for why the change actually resolved the phantom-stock issue.
